industry: Defense Prime Contractor / Aerospace and Missiles
thesis: Lockheed Martin is the world's largest pure-play defense prime, anchored by the F-35 franchise and a record $194B backlog. Surging missile and missile-defense demand, the Golden Dome initiative, and elevated U.S. and allied budgets underpin durable growth and strong free cash flow, supporting a BUY rating as margins recover from 2025 charge-related lows.

drivers: Golden Dome homeland missile-defense architecture drives multi-year, high-margin awards to Missiles and Fire Control and Space
Missile production surge (PAC-3, JASSM, LRASM, THAAD, GMLRS) ramps faster than planned as allies replenish stockpiles
F-35 sustainment and Block 4 / TR-3 upgrades expand a decades-long recurring revenue base
Segment margins recover toward 11%+ as 2025 pension and program charges roll off
Multiple re-rates toward 22x+ forward EPS on record backlog visibility and capital returns

assumptions: Mid-single-digit organic revenue growth with backlog sustained near $190B–$200B
Segment operating margin normalizes to roughly 10.5%–11% as charges abate
Free cash flow of $6.5B–$7.5B funds a growing dividend and consistent buybacks
F-35 deliveries and international demand offset a maturing domestic fighter cycle
Stock trades at 20x–21x forward EPS, in line with large-cap defense primes

risks: U.S. defense budget pressure or continuing resolutions delay procurement and new starts
F-35 program funding, TR-3 software, or engine-upgrade setbacks reduce deliveries and sentiment
Loss of next-generation air-dominance share (F-47 awarded to Boeing) limits long-term aeronautics growth
Fixed-price development cost overruns and further pension or program charges compress margins
Multiple compression to 16x–17x forward EPS on earnings stagnation or political risk

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 Earnings — margin recovery and free cash flow trajectory
Golden Dome architecture awards and missile-defense contract flow
FY2027 Defense Budget Request and NDAA — F-35 and munitions funding visibility
F-35 Lot 19–20 production negotiations and delivery cadence updates
Q4 and Full Year 2026 Earnings — 2027 guidance and backlog update

key_risks: Heavy dependence on U.S. government funding exposes revenue to budget and political cycles
F-35 concentration risk — program delays, funding cuts, or upgrade issues weigh on results
Fixed-price development contracts carry cost-overrun and charge risk
Export-control and geopolitical restrictions can limit or delay international sales
Pension and program accounting charges can distort GAAP earnings and margins
